answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a stake and earn trust slowly through verified work over a long horizon, like tending a garden rather than planting one seed. A Sybil attacker who spins up thousands of fresh identities starts with zero history on every terrace of the market, so their sockpuppets cannot outbid established agents, and slashing the stake when fraud is proven turns cheap identity creation into a losing trade.
